problems.title: Bounded cosine energy does not define the stated prior on an unbounded space
problems.source_location: Section 3.2, Eqs. (1)–(4), PDF p. 5; Section 3.3, PDF p. 6; Appendix A.2.4, PDF p. 17 (Gaussian variational family).
claim: The bounded cosine energy kernel \(e^{-H}\) is treated as a normalized prior on an unbounded space and used with an untruncated Gaussian variational law.
analysis: For a finite graph, \(z_i\in[0,1]\), finite \(d_i>0\) and cosine similarities \(|c_{ij}|\le1\), the written energy satisfies \[0\le H(S;u)\le\sum_{i\in I_G}z_i|N(i)|e^{d_i}+|I_G|\sum_{i=1}^n(1-z_i)e^{d_i}=:M(u)<\infty.\] This bound is independent of the amplitude of \(S\). Consequently \[\int_{\mathbb R^n}e^{-H(S;u)}\,dS\ge e^{-M(u)}\int_{\mathbb R^n}1\,dS=\infty.\] Excluding zero-window null sets or stabilizing the cosine denominator does not supply confinement. The paper’s untruncated Gaussian variational family has unbounded support; restricting only the prior to a bounded pixel box would instead make the variational KL infinite.
result: This is a general normalization obstruction for the written prior. A bounded-support prior would also require matching the Gaussian variational support; treating the kernel as a regularizer is a different interpretation.
assumptions: The finding concerns the stated source version and mathematical or released-code scope.
repair: Use a proper confining/base measure or consistently bounded support, or treat the energy solely as a regularizer. None of these alternatives alone constitutes a repaired full ELBO.
problems.impact_rationale: The stated structural prior has an infinite partition function on its declared support, invalidating the probabilistic/ELBO foundation rather than only a release implementation.
problems.existing_correction_status: The freshly retrieved official paper retains the cited formula or definition. The current author repository head retains the implicated implementation where available. problems.title: The d-update reverses energy signs and is only approximate Gamma conjugacy
problems.source_location: Eq. (14), PDF p. 6; Appendix A.2.3, Eqs. (35)–(43), PDF pp. 16–17; author get_gamma_d.
claim: The update combines log p(d) with log p(S|..), but subsequent equations add the energy terms with the opposite sign.
analysis: The negative energy expands as \(-Ae^{-cd}-Be^{cd}=-A-B+(A-B)cd+O(d^2)\), opposite to the displayed linear sign. With prior shape \(2\), rate \(10^{-4}\), mean latent \(1/2\) and cosine \(1/2\), the off-graph example gives printed rate \(10^{-4}\), versus sign-correct first-order rate \(0.2501\). The original exponential dependence on \(d\) is not Gamma-conjugate. Taylor approximation, MGF clipping and the partition-function problem remain separate limitations.
result: The local sign/approximation issue is supported. Neither the first-order fix nor a one-variable integral is asserted to be the correct full posterior, particularly given the prior-normalization problem.
assumptions: The finding concerns the stated source version and mathematical or released-code scope.
repair: Preserve the negative-energy sign and label the Taylor-Gamma update as approximate; the full consistent prior/posterior still requires analysis.
problems.impact_rationale: The negative-energy sign is reversed in the core latent update and the purported conjugacy is only approximate. This materially changes the stated variational inference derivation.

problems.title: The Beta-KL log-Beta sign changes training gradients
problems.source_location: Appendix A.2.4, Eqs. (54)–(57), PDF p. 17; author losses.py, lines 42–49, and graphseg.py, line 599.
claim: Appendix A.2.4, Eq. (56), PDF p. 17, prints a positive \(\log[\Gamma(\alpha)\Gamma(\beta)/\Gamma(\alpha+\beta)]=\log B(\alpha,\beta)\) term for the variational Beta distribution in the KL defined by Eqs. (54)–(55). The correct variable normalization term has the opposite sign. The active author losses.py function, lines 42–49, called by graphseg.py at line 599, repeats the printed sign.
analysis: Exact Beta KL includes \(\log B(\alpha_0,\beta_0)-\log B(\alpha,\beta)\). The active expression uses a positive sign on the latter term. At \(q=p=\operatorname{Beta}(2,2)\), both parameter gradients are \(-5/3\), whereas a correct KL is minimized there with zero gradient. No additive constant changes this. For \(\operatorname{Beta}(3,3)\) versus \(\operatorname{Beta}(2,2)\), the true KL is \(0.0427712457674\), while the centered source expression is \(-3.17610457910\).
result: The wrong log-Beta sign is present in the paper itself, Eq. (56), and in the called loss function. It changes the core variational objective and its gradients; an unused alternate source function has the correct structure. No performance effect or corrected segmentation score is established.
assumptions: The finding concerns the stated source version and mathematical or released-code scope.
repair: Restore the full Beta-KL sign structure while preserving numerical dtype. This algebraic correction does not establish a repaired model experiment.
problems.impact_rationale: The paper’s Eq. (56), repeated in the active release, reverses the variable log-Beta normalization sign in the core KL derivation. Its nonzero gradient at equal prior/posterior distributions proves a substantive objective error, warranting Major.

problems.title: Entropy and reconstruction normalization alter relative loss weights
problems.source_location: Appendix A.2.4, Eqs. (47) and (51)–(53), PDF p. 17; author losses.py, lines 5–10, and graphseg.py, lines 589 and 603–605.
claim: The objective is presented as a variational decomposition with per-element normalization.
analysis: Gaussian negative entropy has variable term \(-\frac12\sum\log\sigma^2\); the paper uses coefficient \(-1\) and the active code \(-2\), while the other terms retain their own weights. Reconstruction is averaged and then divided again by element count \(N\). For unit residuals and \(N=4,8,16\), this yields \(0.25,0.125,0.0625\), whereas the stated half-per-element quadratic is \(0.5\). These are parameter-dependent relative-weight and size effects, not one additive constant.
result: The source objective has parameter-dependent relative-weight and batch-size differences. These cannot all be absorbed into an additive constant or common scalar.
assumptions: The finding concerns the stated source version and mathematical or released-code scope.
repair: Use the intended one-half entropy coefficient and one declared reconstruction normalization; full probabilistic consistency and retraining outcomes remain open.
problems.impact_rationale: This establishes the stated local correction or limitation. A consequential failure of the paper's central result has not been demonstrated.

problems.title: Returned SoftDice is replaced by label-optimized hard Dice
problems.source_location: Appendix B.1, PDF p. 19; author metrics.py, lines 143–205, and find_best_dice_threshold, lines 5–38.
claim: The paper defines SoftDice using continuous probabilities and a squared denominator; the release overwrites its soft_dice variable with the best hard-threshold score on the supplied labels.
analysis: For probabilities \((0.49,0.48)\), labels \((1,0)\), and stabilizer \(10^{-6}\), the paper's squared-denominator SoftDice is \(0.6664402132\). Hard F1 at threshold \(0.5\) is zero; searching thresholds \(0,0.01,\ldots,1\) selects \(0.49\) and returns hard Dice \(1\). The source overwrites its soft_dice variable with that label-optimized hard score; its earlier soft value also has a different linear denominator.
result: This confirms an evaluation-function semantics error. It does not establish that the published tables used this code or prove test-set leakage; historical predictions/calls are unavailable.
assumptions: The finding concerns the stated source version and mathematical or released-code scope.
repair: Compute the stated continuous SoftDice separately from hard-threshold metrics. If a threshold is selected, do so under a separately defined validation protocol.
